title: Brain Switches

mascot.name: Chip
mascot.greeting: Hi! Let's meet a tiny switch.

recap: A neuron is a tiny yes/no switch.
It listens to clues and adds them up.
Lots of switches together can spot a cat.

sections.heading: A tiny yes/no switch
sections.bigIdea: A neuron is a tiny switch that says yes or no.
sections.bodyMarkdown: Think of a **neuron** as a light switch. It listens to clues. If enough clues say yes, it turns on.

teen.add: Each clue has a **weight**: how much the switch cares about it.

jargonBuster.simpleExplanation: A tiny switch that says yes or no.

more.title: Who thought of this?
more.bodyMarkdown: Scientists built the first one in the 1950s.

diagram.caption: How a switch decides
diagram.alt: Three steps: clues come in, they add up, the switch turns on.

sections.heading: Switches work as a team
sections.bigIdea: Many switches together can spot a cat.
sections.bodyMarkdown: One switch is simple. A big **team** of switches can spot ears, whiskers and tails.

teen.body: TEEN-ONLY: in a network, each layer of switches passes its answers to the next layer.

interactiveWidget.goal: See how clues turn a switch on.
hints: Chip's hint: try turning up one clue.
